1. (Currently amended) An ultrasonic surgical instrument assembly comprising: a handpiece; a transducer or generator of ultrasonic mechanical vibrations disposed in said handpiece; a probe attached to a distal end of said handpiece and operatively connected to said transducer or generator; and a light source attached to said handpiece so as to direct at least visible electromagnetic radiation along the probe towards a surgical site distal of the probe, wherein said light source is positioned to provide illumination independent of said transducer or generator operation.

2. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 1, further comprising a power supply mounted at least indirectly to said handpiece and operatively connected to said light source, wherein said power supply is separate from and independent of power supplied to said transducer or generator.

3. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 2 wherein said power supply includes a coil disposed about a power cable feeding said transducer or generator, and wherein said coil is operatively connected to said light source through a separate electrical circuit.

4. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 3 wherein said power supply further includes a slow-drain capacitor operatively connected to said coil for providing energy or power to said light source for a predetermined period of time after termination of power conduction through said cable.

19. (Currently amended) A surgical method comprising: providing a surgical instrument having a handpiece, a transducer or generator of ultrasonic mechanical vibrations disposed in said handpiece and a probe attached to a distal end of said handpiece and operatively connected to said transducer or generator; providing a light source; applying a fastener to said handpiece to attach said light source thereto so that light from said light source is directable along said probe; operating said surgical instrument to apply ultrasonic vibratory energy to a surgical site; during the operating of said surgical instrument, conducting electrical energy from a power supply to said light source; and during the operating of said surgical instrument and the conducting of said electrical energy, illuminating said surgical site with light from said source, wherein said light source operation is independent of said transducer or generator operation.
